You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Background is uniform (e.g. 7); the grid contains several filled axis-aligned color rectangles, sometimes with isolated foreign-color intrusions inside and scattered outside. Restore intrusions inside a clearly continued rectangle to that rectangle’s color; change unrelated external speckles to background. Preserve every coherent rectangle even when it shares a color with noise or another object. Use repeated rows/columns and full rectangle bounds; scan all rows carefully (in the solved test, a 9 rectangle at left spanned rows 17–20, not just 17–18). Demo: background 7, color-3 block(s) and color-0 rectangles; embedded 9 inside the 3 block became 3, 9/2/6 stray marks outside were cleared, and foreign marks inside 0 rectangle became 0. Solved test had 9 rectangles at r0–2 c11–13, r4–10 c6–7, r12–17 c5–11, r16–22 c13–15, r17–20 c0–1; 5 rectangles at r4–10 c2–3, r4–10 c9–12, r22–23 c7–10. Restore any non-object intrusions within these footprints and clear remaining isolated colors to 7. This pattern solved exactly.

More confirmed recurrence evidence (0-based inclusive bounds): Demo 1 had background 1 and color-6 rectangles at r2–5,c3–7; r7–13,c1–6; r17–21,c2–5; r24–26,c6–8. Demo 2 had background 5 and rectangles color 4 at r2–3,c4–5 and r3–8,c11–14, plus color 2 at r3–9,c25–27. Other colors (including 0,1,6,9 and sporadic foreign-color marks) were changed to background unless inside one of those rectangle footprints, where they were restored to the rectangle color. Thus objects can have different colors in the same input; identify filled rectangular footprints from repeated rows/columns, then restore all cells inside and clear all noise outside.

Solved fresh test with background 0: rectangles were color 8 at r2–5,c2–6; r3–6,c9–12; r8–9,c7–13; and color 1 at r0–6,c14–16; r1–2,c22–27; r4–9,c18–23; r4–8,c25–29; r7–11,c2–5. Successful output filled each footprint and cleared all other nonzero noise to 0. Important bounds lesson from wrong attempts: the rectangle r4–9,c18–23 included row-9 intrusions at c19 and c22 (must restore them); the left-lower 1 rectangle extended through row 11. Do not stop a rectangle at a partially corrupted row if its columns clearly continue; conversely do not extend beyond a fully-background gap.

Confirmed fresh recurrence task-72bfad94 (background 9), solved after correcting two under-sized rectangle bounds. Restore all non-background intrusions within each rectangle and set all external speckles to 9. 0-based inclusive rectangles: color 8 at r3-8,c1-5; r5-8,c7-10; r4-7,c12-15; r2-4,c22-25; r7-13,c21-22; r11-15,c3-8; r17-18,c8-13; r18-19,c19-22; r21-24,c14-18; r19-24,c0-2. Color 4 at r1-2,c8-13; r10-15,c11-16; r8-14,c18-19; r20-24,c4-7. First answer was wrong because it clipped the upper-right 8 rectangle at r3 instead of r4 and the right-side narrow 8 rectangle at r10 instead of r13; checking consecutive rows showed both color columns continued. This confirms the task-72bfad94 rule: identify the full rectangular footprint from repeated row/column structure despite noisy cells; fill intrusions with the rectangle's color; clear all other isolated colors to uniform background.

Another confirmed test instance solved exactly (background 6, 20x29). Restore these complete rectangle footprints, inclusive 0-based bounds; every other cell becomes 6: color 2 at r0-3,c0-1; r2-8,c6-8; r5-11,c1-2; r6-8,c10-14; r6-7,c27-28; r13-19,c13-19; r15-19,c3-4. Color 4 at r0-4,c12-14; r0-3,c16-21; r0-2,c23-26; r15-17,c7-11; r17-18,c21-24. Color 5 at r5-11,c16-22; r9-13,c24-28; r10-11,c5-7; r16-17,c26-28. All other 0/9/2/4/5 speckles were either replaced by their rectangle color when inside a footprint or cleared to background outside. Important boundary lesson: the color-2 rectangle at r2-4,c6-8 continues directly through r5-8,c6-8; the uniform block is one larger r2-8,c6-8 rectangle. Preserve connected adjoining rows as a single full footprint when same columns continue, even if an intrusion appears within it.")]
